index_record.dataset_generation_caption:
The figure presents a hierarchical classification of metastructure unit cells, organized into three main categories: (a) Unit Cells (2D), (b) Complex/Hybrid Unit Cells, and (c) Multi-Unit Patterns. The overall layout is divided into three vertically aligned sections labeled (a), (b), and (c), each containing a top-level rectangular box connected via blue arrows to subordinate boxes representing specific structural types. Each structural type is accompanied by a corresponding black-and-white geometric icon illustrating its physical form.

In section (a), 'Unit Cells (2D)', five primary 2D unit cell types are listed: Re-entrant, Chiral, Anti-chiral, Kagome, and Rotating Structures. These are arranged vertically beneath the main header, each connected by a blue arrow from the parent node. The icons next to them depict their characteristic shapes: a re-entrant structure with inward-pointing angles, chiral and anti-chiral structures with asymmetric, mirror-image forms, a Kagome lattice resembling a star of David, and rotating structures composed of four rotated squares forming a cross-like pattern.

Section (b), 'Complex/Hybrid Unit Cells', branches into three main subtypes: Hierarchical Metastucture, Fractals, and Interlaced Metastucture. The first two are direct children of the main category, while 'Interlaced Metastucture' further subdivides into 'Self-Similar' and 'Heterogeneous'. The associated icons show a hexagonal structure with internal dots for hierarchical, a nested hexagonal fractal for fractals, a self-similar hexagonal pattern for self-similar, and a star-shaped heterogeneous design for heterogeneous.

Section (c), 'Multi-Unit Patterns', outlines four methods for arranging unit cells: Distribution and Connection, Periodicity and Gradient, Interlocking, and Wedge Gradient. These are arranged horizontally under the main header, each linked by a blue arrow. The icons illustrate these arrangements: irregularly distributed hexagons for distribution and connection, a regular honeycomb grid for periodicity and gradient, interlocked hexagons with internal patterns for interlocking, and a 3D-like stepped hexagonal array for wedge gradient.

All text boxes are white with dark teal borders and black sans-serif font. Arrows are solid blue lines with arrowheads indicating directionality. Icons are monochromatic, using thick black lines to define shapes, and are placed immediately to the right of their corresponding text labels. The figure visually communicates a taxonomy of metastructure designs, progressing from simple 2D unit cells to complex hybrid forms and finally to multi-unit assembly strategies.
